9.title: LoopFi
9.desc: LoopFi is a command-line interface application built with Java and Spring Shell for managing personal finances. It offers comprehensive features including multi-account transaction management, detailed reporting, and spending analysis tools while providing an intuitive and streamlined user experience.

8.title: Spark Launcher
8.desc: Spark Launcher is a specialized game launcher application developed in Java and Kotlin, designed to streamline the game launching process. The project provides a customizable interface for managing and launching various games, featuring automatic updates, profile management, and game configuration tools. Built with modern development practices, Spark Launcher offers a seamless gaming experience while maintaining robust security measures and efficient resource management.

7.title: Canyon Wolf Website
7.desc: Canyon Wolf Website is a personal portfolio website built using modern web technologies including Next.js, React, and TypeScript. The site showcases professional experience, technical projects, and development skills through a clean, responsive interface. Features include dynamic project cards, detailed work experience sections, and seamless navigation. The website demonstrates proficiency in front-end development while serving as a comprehensive professional portfolio tailored to gaming.

6.title: VacuumBreak
6.desc: VacuumBreak is an open-source tool designed for automated server backups, specifically tailored for Spigot-based Minecraft servers. Written in Java, it offers customizable backup configurations, including options for backup frequency, snapshot limits, and inclusion of specific game dimensions like the Nether and The End. VacuumBreak ensures seamless server management by providing a reliable solution for safeguarding game data. The project is licensed under GPL-3.0 and is actively maintained, with plans for future enhancements such as cloud storage integration and advanced permission systems.

5.title: Lubbock Covid-19 Information Chatbot
5.desc: This project was created as an introduction to dialog agents. The chatbot provides information related to COVID-19 to a user. The information gathered for this agent was obtained from Texas Tech University, the City of Lubbock Health Department, and Texas Department of State Health Services. The agent was created in Google Dialogflow and Actions for Google Assistant to provide an excellent user experience, and can be utilized either in browser, through Dialogflow Phone Gateway, or on any Google Assistant enabled device.

4.title: Los Angeles Traffic Prediction Bayesian Network
4.desc: This project was created as an introduction to bayesian networks. The network was created using data obtained from NOAA, and The City of Los Angeles. This traffic prediction network simplifies many factors that play a role in traffic analysis.

3.title: Squeeze-It AI Agent
3.desc: This project was created for Introduction to Logic Programming. The Binary Sudoku Solver uses Clingo, MKAtoms, Python, and TKInter to solve a binary sudoku puzzle. TKInter is use for building the GUI and MKAtoms creates an atom for use in Clingo. Clingo (the chosen answer set solver) utilizes a list of rules in order to solve the puzzle.

TKInter is use for building the GUI and MKAtoms creates an atom for use in Clingo. Clingo (the chosen answer set solver) utilizes a list of rules in order to solve the puzzle.

1.title: Unix Find Utility
1.desc:
This project was created for Concepts of Operating Systems. This project uses C to recreate the Unix find utility. The implemented functionalities, and syntax for these functionalities are listed in this project's ReadMe file. 
The project utilizes System headers (sys/types.h, sys/stat.h), dirent.h, and others to list out files that the user wants to find and any other arguments included. The output of the project will be a list of files matching the included arguments.

0.title: New York Airport Annual Enplanements
0.desc:
This project was created for Introduction to Database Systems. The New York Airport Annual Enplanements project utilizes a LAMP stack, and JavaScript components to display New York state airport data from the Annual Enplanements in NYS Airports: Beginning 1997 dataset published by New York State.
The project utilizes many SQL commands to generate and import the dataset as well as display the data in the JavaScript Components.
